newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Forestry analysts still cautious after SCA.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Forestry analysts still cautious after SCA.

text.p: Swedish forestry major SCA posted higher than expected profits for the first half of 1997, boosting hopes that the next half will also be good for the sector, though fears for 1998 remain.
Mirroring other Swedish and Finnish forestry companies, SCA reported higher volumes and benefits from weaker local currencies on Wednesday although prices have seen very little improvement.

It posted a 35 percent rise in profit after financial items to 2.25 billion crowns ($280.4 million), which included a capital gain of 425 million crowns from selling shares in AB Industrivarden. The market had expected a profit of 2.01 billion.

"The main difference was better results from its packaging and graphic paper businesses," said Paribas analyst Hubert de Marliare, who intended to lift his full year forecast to about four billion crowns from 3.87 billion on the report.
"I believe this is a good year for paper stocks to outperform the market but next year could be a more difficult one...with larger capacity coming on in Asia that could put pressure on pulp prices."
SCA's share dipped on the report, down 1.5 crowns to 194.5 at 1030 GMT but the Stockholm general index was down 1.34 percent.
"We are seeing some profit taking in forestry stocks after recent gains," said one Stockholm broker.
SCA posted a four percent rise in six month sales to 29.33 billion crowns with a six percent rise in the second quarter.

"This is attributable to the effect of reduced average prices affecting invoicing adversely by eight percent, being offset by strong volume increases of 10 percent and more favourable currency rates of two percent," said SCA, which forecast a continuing but slow recovery in Europe in 1997.

Sales in its graphic paper unit rose two percent to 8.11 billion crowns with volumes up 10 percent and prices down nine percent while packaging sales edged up to 7.30 billion crowns from 7.13 billion with prices down 11 percent but volumes rising 10.

SCA said sales in its hygiene products division rose nine percent to 13.05 billion crowns with an 11 percent growth in volumes and two percent positive effect from currency moves and it expected continuing strong demand.
"It was a reasonably strong report," said Morgan Stanley analyst Mads Asprem.
"But I don't think we have seen any indication in any of these reports that the second half of the year or next year will see any real improvement in the sector."
Analysts said reports from Finland's Metsa-Serla and Sweden's Stora last week were more bullish on the forestry sector than those released by SCA or Finnish Enso.
Swedish forester AssiDoman was also fairly optimistic as it posted a higher than expected result on Tuesday, saying it expected a continued strengthening of trends in the forestry industry in 1997.
AssiDoman shares rose seven crowns to 247 on Wednesday, partly lifted by S-E-Banken upgrading its trading recommendation on the share to 'buy' from 'outperform'.

"In the past three months we have been aggressive buyers of forestry shares and AssiDoman is the Swedish company we consider the most interesting in the long and short term," S-E-Banken analyst Karl-Johan Krigstrom told Reuters.
He said S-E-Banken was also positive on Finnish company UPM Kymmene and Metsa-Serla.
"If we put together a forestry portfolio we would include AssiDoman, UPM Kymmene och Metsa-Serla," Krigstrom said.
The last major Swedish forestry group, MoDo, and Finland's UPM-Kymmene are due to report first half earnings on August 14.
-- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017 ($ = 8.024 Swedish Crowns)
